headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: plano can ingest and forward content while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list with no isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest B. B exposes file input via config.yaml and an OpenAI-compatible API, and its broad egress means content it processes could be forwarded. Because the pairwise bridge is undocumented and A is non-runnable, this is an inferred interaction, not direct evidence.
conditions: IF A is manually copied into B's config or prompt inputs, B may treat it as instruction-bearing content.
IF B is deployed with permissive prompt parsing, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Restrict B to structured inputs only.
Add a prompt-injection filter before B forwards content.
Keep A as a static reference list, not an input source.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all copied content.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted message schemas in B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not a leakage source. B touches logs, traces, and metrics and has broad network egress, but the profiles do not show shared storage or sensitive classes flowing from A to B. The main risk is limited to accidental exposure of operational telemetry if copied into B.
conditions: IF operational logs or traces are pasted into B, they may be transmitted to external services.
IF A is repurposed to hold sensitive content, the pairwise leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not paste logs into B unless redacted.
Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Review B outbound destinations.
requires-engineering: add DLP redaction before B egress.
requires-engineering: segregate telemetry from user content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can call APIs and read config.yaml, but supports only one instance and has no subprocesses or browser automation. With no shared writable target shown, direct capability conflict is unlikely.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same config.yaml or shared mutable resource, write contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, conflicts become more plausible.
mitigations: Use separate config files.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Run only one B instance per resource.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state.
requires-engineering: isolate per-agent workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume external content through its API and may act on it as routing or planning input, while A is a static curated list with no verification or execution layer. If A-derived content is copied into B, B may treat it as authoritative without a validation step. The interaction is inferred, but the downstream misrouting blast radius can affect multiple work products.
conditions: IF content from A is used as source material for B outputs, B may propagate errors.
IF B is configured to act on unverified prompts, cascading mistakes can reach downstream tasks.
mitigations: Require human review of B outputs.
Mark A content as non-authoritative.
Add a verification step before B acts.
requires-engineering: attach source citations to copied content.
requires-engineering: block autonomous actions from unverified inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either profile. A has no touched data classes and B only lists operational telemetry classes, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway in the pair. The other agent is not separately cited because no cross-agent compliance flow is shown.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data into B, compliance review is required.
IF either profile gains residency or retention constraints, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of B.
Review retention settings.
requires-engineering: add residency controls.
requires-engineering: add audit logging for regulated flows.
